This appeal is filed by the plaintiff in O.S. No.11/2012 on the file of the learned Civil Judge, Ankola challenging the judgment and decree passed in RA No.15/2017 by the learned Senior Civil Judge,
Ankola dated 12.08.2017.
2. I refer the parties as their rank before the trial Court.
3. It was the case of the plaintiff/appellant that one Govind Timmanna Nayak and Smt. Devamma Nayak were parents of the plaintiffs and defendant No.1 and they had constituted joint family.
The suit schedule properties as well as the properties acquired by the Government, were ancestral and joint family properties of late Govind Timmanna Nayak, his wife, plaintiff and defendant No.1.
The plaintiff and defendant No.1 along with their parents have been enjoying suit schedule properties as joint family properties.

2 death, defendant No.1 had been managing the suit properties and in some of the property records the name of defendant No.1 was entered but they are also joint family properties.

sentences.text: Defendant No.1 was mismanaging suit properties so also refused to share the benefit of lands with plaintiff.

Hence,
she sought for partition and separate possession of her share but defendant No.1 refused to effect partition and allot share to the plaintiff.
Therefore, she was constrained to file the suit.
With these averments prayed for partition and separate possession of half share in the suit properties.
4. The contentions of defendant No.1 before the trial Court were that, the plaintiff was born prior to 1953 and she was not a coparcener to the family.
She had no right over the suit properties.
The Government had awarded compensation in the name of defendant No.1 for the lands which were acquired.
Some of the suit properties are self acquired properties of defendant No.1.
So also some of the properties were self acquired properties of his mother- Smt.Devamma.

During her life time, she had executed gift deed in respect of some of the properties belonging to her in favour of defendant No.1 and by virtue of the same, defendant No.1 became absolute owner of the suit properties.
With these reasons, he prayed for dismissing the suit.
5. During the pendency of the suit, defendant Nos.2(a) to (c) have been got impleaded as legal heirs of Smt. Seeta @ Beeramma, who is alleged to be one of the daughters of Govind Nayak.
They also claimed 1/3rd share in the suit schedule properties.
6. From the rival contentions of the parties, the trial Court has framed the issues.
7. The plaintiff, on he behalf examined herself as PW-1 and got marked Exs.P-1 to P-29.

The defendant examined DWs.1 to 3 and got marked Exs.D1 to D-11.
8.

The trial Court after hearing both the parties, appreciating the pleadings and evidence on record,
decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 15.02.2013 and held that, the suit schedule properties and other properties acquired by the Government belonging to Govind Nayak, are the joint family properties.

It has also held that, the mother of defendant No.2(a) to (c) by name Smt.
Seeta @ Beeramma was not the daughter of late Govind Nayak and Devamma and therefore they are not entitled for any share and the plaintiff is entitled for half share in the suit properties.
9.

Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree, defendant No.1 preferred appeal in RA No.15/2017 and defendant Nos.2(a) to (c) have filed appeal in RA No.20/2017 before the Court of Senior Civil Judge at Ankola.
The learned Senior Civil Judge, heard the matter and on re- appreciation of the evidence passed the impugned judgment on 12.08.2017 dismissing both the appeals.
However, the shares were modified and 1/4th share was allotted to the plaintiff and 3/4th share was allotted to defendant No.1.

The first appellate Court has held that defendant Nos.2(a) to (c) are not members of the family of the plaintiff and defendant No.1.
10.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed in RA No.15/2017, the plaintiff preferred this second appeal.

sentences.text: I have heard the arguments of the learned advocate for the appellant.
However, none appear on behalf of the respondent and argued the matter.
13. My findings on the above substantial questions of law for the following reasons.
14. The genealogy of the family of the plaintiff and defendant No1.1 is not in dispute.
It is admitted by both the plaintiff and defendant No.1 that they are the children of late Govind Nayak.

Both the Courts below held that defendant Nos.2(a) to (c) have utterly failed to establish that late Govind Nayak and Devamma had another daughter by name Seeta @ Beeramma and defendant Nos.2(a) to (c) were the grandchildren of late Govind Nayak.
Defendant No.2(a) to (c) did not file any second appeal and they have accepted the concurrent findings of the trial Court as well as the first appellate Court.
Therefore, there is no need to consider the same.
15. Both the courts below have concurrently held that the suit schedule properties are joint family properties of late Govind Nayak.
Defendant No.1 was also not able to prove that Devamma had executed Will in respect of some of the properties in his favour.

Defendant No.1 has not filed any appeal challenging the impugned judgment and he had accepted that all the suit schedule properties are joint family properties including the land acquired by the Government.

16. Learned advocate for the appellant vehemently contended that the trial Court has rightly held that the suit schedule properties are joint family properties and the plaintiff, being a member of the family, is entitled for equal share and accordingly allotted half share in the suit schedule properties including the amount of compensation awarded for acquiring the land by the Government.

However, the first appellate Court relying on the judgment in the case of Prakash (supra) held that the plaintiff is entitled for  share in the share belonging to late Govind Nayak since she is not entitled for share on par with a son, though Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act has been amended.
The said finding is erroneous.

He has further submitted that, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma and others reported in (2020) 9 SCC 1, the plaintiff being the daughter of late Govind Nayak is entitled for equal share as that of a son i.e. half share in the suit property.

sentences.text: It appears in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Vineeta Sharma (supra), defendant No.1 found that, there was no need of re- agitating the matter.
Accordingly, has not appeared and argued the matter.

In the case of Vineeta Sharma(supra), it is held by the Hon'be Supreme Court that amendment to Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 is retrospective effect and it will come into force from the date of passing of the Hindu Succession Act.
Thereby a female heir is entitled for equal share in the suit properties with that of a male member.
In view of the said law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the appellant is entitled for half share in the suit properties and defendant No.1 is entitled for the remaining half share.
The law laid by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Prakash(supra), has been over ruled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
The appellate Court on the basis of the law laid down in the case of Prakash(supra), granted 1/4th share to the plaintiff in the suit schedule properties.

In the case of Vineeta Sharma(supra), the larger bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that, Amendment to Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act is retrospective in effect and the female heirs who are born prior to 1956 or onwards are entitled for equal share to that of a male heir.

It was held as under:
" Section 6 of HS Act, 1956 deals with devolution of interest in coparcenary property of a Hindu family governed by the Mitakshara law.
The originally enacted provision of Section 6 excluded the rule of succession concerning Mitakshara coparcenary property.
It provided that the interest of a coparcener male Hindu who died after the commencement of the 1956 Act, shall be governed by survivorship upon the surviving members of the coparcenary.

The exception was provided by the proviso to Section 6 that if the deceased had left surviving a female relative specified in Class I of he Schedule or a male relative specified in that Class who claims through such female relative, the interest of such coparcener shall devolve by testamentary or intestate succession, as the case may be, in order to ascertain the share of deceased coparcener, the partition has to be deemed before his death.
Explanation II disentitle the separated person to make any claim in case of intestate succession.
The substituted provisions of Section 6(1) of the HS Act, 1956 provide that on and from the commencement of the 2005 Amendment Act, the daughter s conferred the right of a coparcener.
Section 6(1)(a) makes daughter by birth a coparcener "in her own right" and "in the same manner as the son".
Section 6(1)(a) contains the concept of the unobstructed heritage of Mitakshara coparcenary, which is by virtue of birth.
Section 6(1)(b) confers the same rights in the coparcenary property "as she would have had if she had been a son".

The conferral of right is by birth, and the rights are given in the same manner with incidents of coparcenary as that of a son and she is treated as a coparcener in the same manner with the same rights as if she had been a son at the time of birth."
18. In view of the aforesaid law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the appellant/plaintiff is entitled for half share in the suit schedule properties.
Accordingly, I answer the substantial questions of law in favour of the appellant and against the respondent No.1 and pass the following ORDER Appeal is partly allowed.
The share of the appellant/plaintiff is modified.
